title: Log House Museum

services.name: Schedule a Tour
services.desc: The Log House Museum is a City of Seattle Historic Landmark and is located one block from Alki Beach Park, known to Coast Salish people as sbaqʷabqs or Prairie Point. It was built as an outbuilding to the Historic Fir Lodge (Alki Homestead Restaurant) in 1903-1904. Today, it is the home of the Southwest Seattle Historical Society. Read more here. Admission: The museum offers free admission. A suggested donation of $5 is encouraged and gladly accepted. Directions: The Log House Museum is located one block from Alki Beach. Street parking only. blurb: Alki was first called sbaqʷabqs. It means prairie in Lushootseed, the language of Coast Salish people. It describes how this place looked-grassy plains and scattered stands of fir trees.
